key_insight: For OITE questions, the clinical vignette—not the image—is the main driver of LLM performance; removing the vignette causes the largest accuracy drop.
clinical_relevance: In medical exam-style QA, these results suggest LLMs may rely heavily on text context and answer-option patterns, so clinicians should be cautious about assuming genuine image-based or case-based reasoning.
method: Evaluated 8 LLMs: 3 open-source Ministral-3 models and 5 proprietary models.
Tested 792 Orthopaedic In-Training Examination questions from 2020–2024.
Sequentially removed question components (vignette, images, question stem, answer choices) and compared accuracy across conditions.
evidence_signal: Using paired analyses on 792 OITE questions, full-context accuracy fell sharply when the vignette was removed, while removing images alone did not significantly change performance for any model.
watch_item: This is an exam-performance study, so higher accuracy may not translate to safe or reliable clinical reasoning in real-world care.
paper_title: Do Large Language Models Use the Clinical Vignette? A Question Ablation Study on the Orthopaedic In-Training Examination
